reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let d,N be natural numbers with N>0, (Omega,m,P) a probability space, and F=(F_t)_{t>=0} a filtration subordinate to m. Require F to be right-continuous and every set A with P(A)=0 to be F_t-measurable for every t>=0. Set S={x in R^d: ||x||=1}, using the usual Euclidean norm, coordinates and real inner product.

For each i in Fin N let B_i:[0,infinity) x Omega -> R^d satisfy the following conditions: B_i(0,omega)=0 for every omega; every finite collection of its increments over pairwise disjoint half-open intervals (s_j,t_j], s_j<=t_j, is independent; for s<t and every continuous real linear functional ell, ell(B_i(t)-B_i(s)) has centered Gaussian law of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; its paths are continuous P-almost surely; B_i(t) is strongly F_t-measurable; and B_i(t)-B_i(s) is independent of F_s for s<=t. There is no assumption of independence between different B_i.

Let X_i,Y_i:[0,infinity) x Omega -> S be jointly measurable and strongly progressive, for each i. Strong progressivity here means that for every u>=0, the map (s,omega)->X_i(s,omega), respectively Y_i(s,omega), restricted to [0,u] x Omega is strongly measurable for Borel([0,u]) times F_u. Let b_X,b_Y:[0,infinity) x S^N x S^N x Fin N -> R^d have continuous dependence on (t,x,y) for each i on the entire indicated domain. Fix a constant real lambda>=0.

Use the supplied continuous representative I_T(eta,B)(t,omega) of the scalar L2 Ito integral on horizon T>0. This is a definition with mathematical identification supplied by the context, not merely a name: elementary coefficients are bounded and strongly measurable at their left grid endpoints; the elementary integral is sum_r c_r(omega)[B(min(t_{r+1},t),omega)-B(min(t_r,t),omega)], and its horizon-T process substitutes min(t,T). The canonical elementary integrands converge to eta in L2(P x ds); their terminal stochastic sums converge in L2(P) to the specified terminal completion, with an approximation-independence characterization. The process body is zero on its specified null bad set and otherwise the atTop path limit of these elementary processes. For each t<=T it agrees P-almost surely with the terminal completion at horizon T of eta(s,omega)1_{s<t}. It has continuous paths on [0,T]. The supplied uniqueness theorem identifies continuous strongly adapted versions simultaneously at every time in that interval outside one null set. These characterizations determine the required integral semantics without expanding every internal dyadic/truncation choice.

Write X(s,omega)=(X_l(s,omega))_l and Y(s,omega)=(Y_l(s,omega))_l, and B_i^j for the j-th coordinate of B_i. For Z=X or Y the supplied noise integrand is exactly
 eta^Z_{i,k,j}(s,omega)=sqrt(2 lambda)[1_{k=j}-Z_i^j(s,omega)Z_i^k(s,omega)].
Its projected noise column is e_j-Z_i^j Z_i. It is packaged as a progressive L2 integrand for P times upTo(T). The time measure upTo(t) is the comap by NNReal.toReal of Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,t]. The supplied prefix integral of q is int q(s,omega) d upTo(t)(s).

Assume that for every T>0, P-almost surely, simultaneously for every nonnegative t<=T, every i in Fin N and every k in Fin d, BOTH identities hold:
 X_i^k(t,omega)=X_i^k(0,omega)+int_0^t [b_X^k(s,X(s,omega),Y(s,omega),i)-lambda(d-1)X_i^k(s,omega)] ds + sum_{j in Fin d} I_T(eta^X_{i,k,j},B_i^j)(t,omega),
 Y_i^k(t,omega)=Y_i^k(0,omega)+int_0^t [b_Y^k(s,X(s,omega),Y(s,omega),i)-lambda(d-1)Y_i^k(s,omega)] ds + sum_{j in Fin d} I_T(eta^Y_{i,k,j},B_i^j)(t,omega).
The actual scalar driver is the SAME B_i^j in the paired equations. The exceptional set may depend on T, but within each horizon is common to all times, indices and both identities.

For real t set t_+=max(t,0), viewed as a nonnegative real, and define
 delta_i(t,omega)=X_i(t_+,omega)-Y_i(t_+,omega),
 D(t)=N^{-1} sum_i int_Omega ||delta_i(t,omega)||^2 dP(omega),
 R4(t)=N^{-1} sum_i int_Omega ||delta_i(t,omega)||^4 dP(omega),
 L(t)=2 N^{-1} sum_i int_Omega <delta_i(t,omega),b_X(t_+,X(t_+,omega),Y(t_+,omega),i)-b_Y(t_+,X(t_+,omega),Y(t_+,omega),i)>_R dP(omega),
 G(t)=L(t)-2 lambda(d-3)D(t)-lambda R4(t).
The indices in these sums range over Fin N. The expectation integrals are ordinary real integrals with respect to P. Both d-1 and d-3 are real subtractions after casting d to R, not truncated subtraction in Nat; N^{-1} is a real reciprocal.

The theorem concludes all of the following together: G is continuous on R and locally integrable for real Lebesgue measure; for every a,b>=0, D(b)-D(a)=int_a^b G(t)dt, using the oriented interval integral without an a<=b premise; D is absolutely continuous on [0,T] for every T>=0; D has classical derivative G(t) at every real t>0; and D has within-[0,infinity) derivative G(0) at zero, namely the right derivative.

The global continuity/local-integrability conclusions refer to the specified clamped real-time extension. No assertion D'=G at negative time is made. This is an implication about supplied processes satisfying the integral identities, not a process-existence result. No d>0 or d>=2 premise, drift tangency, equality of initial states, cross-particle independence or unnamed numerical constant is imposed.
objects: Probability space and nonnegative-time filtration; separately standard Euclidean Brownian processes B_i; two sphere-valued process families X_i/Y_i; continuous joint drift fields b_X/b_Y; fixed lambda>=0; specified continuous L2 Ito integral representatives; expectation functions delta,D,R4,L,G.
domains: d,N in Nat with N>0; i in Fin N and k,j in Fin d; unit sphere in EuclideanSpace R (Fin d). Processes have NNReal time; D,R4,L,G have real time clamped by t.toNNReal=max(t,0). Strong progressivity uses Borel([0,u]) times F_u. P supplies expectation measure; real Lebesgue measure supplies interval/local integrability.
quantifiers: For every d,N,Omega,m,filtration,P, assuming N>0; then every B satisfying the separate Brownian predicates, usual-condition proof, X/Y with joint measurability/progressivity, b_X/b_Y with per-index joint continuity, and lambda>=0. SDE premise: forall positive T, P-a.e. omega, forall NNReal t<=T, forall i,k, BOTH equations. Conclusions: all a,b>=0 and T>=0, all real derivative times t>0, and the right derivative at zero.
assumptions: N>0. Each B_i has pointwise zero start, independent increments over every finite disjoint interval family, centered Gaussian scalar projections with variance (t-s)||ell||^2, a.e. continuous paths, strong F_t adaptation and future increments independent of F_s. F is right-continuous and contains every P-null set at each time. X/Y are jointly measurable and strongly progressive. Both drifts are jointly continuous in time and both configurations for each i. lambda is constant nonnegative. The paired integral identities hold simultaneously a.s. on each positive finite horizon. No cross-particle independence, dimension lower bound, tangency or initial-equality assumption.
conclusion: For the explicitly defined delta,D,R4,L,G: Continuous G and LocallyIntegrable G volume on R; D(b)-D(a)=oriented integral_a^b G for all a,b>=0; absolute continuity of D on every [0,T]; HasDerivAt D (G(t)) t for all real t>0; HasDerivWithinAt D (G(0)) (Ici 0) 0.
scopes: SDE null set may depend on positive horizon T, but is uniform in t<=T and finite indices and both systems. Scalar driver B_i^j is identical in both equations. Moment derivative conclusions hold pointwise for every positive time, with a right derivative at zero; no negative-time derivative identity is asserted. G continuity/local integrability holds on all real time for the clamped extension.
constant_dependencies: Only N^{-1}, factor 2, d cast to R, constant lambda>=0, and unit sphere radius. SDE curvature drift is lambda(d-1)Z; derivative correction is 2lambda(d-3)D+lambda R4. No unspecified horizon-, dimension-, state- or particle-dependent constant.
